# TerraScan: transferring a Sentinel-2 land-use classifier from Europe to India

*Technical report (step 8.11). Generated by `src/tech_report.py` from `results/`; every number below names its file.*

## Abstract

Land-use classifiers trained on EuroSAT reach about {eurosat_low}-{eurosat_high} test accuracy on European Sentinel-2
images, consistent with the {published_acc} reported by the dataset's authors. On {n_india_test} hand-labelled patches
from two held-out areas in Gujarat, India, the model picked for India (EfficientNet-B0) falls to {india_acc_before}
(mean ± std, 3 seeds). Fine-tuning on {n_finetune} labelled Indian patches from three other areas raises this to
{india_acc_after} (`results/india_after.json`). Further attempts to improve it ({phase8_list}) are reported with decision rules fixed before each
run: {phase8_summary}. A change map of Ahmedabad 2018-2026 over-reports
change: {real_rate} of {change_n_pairs} randomly checked changed squares held up. The full inference pipeline also runs in
a web browser and matches the Python pipeline on {parity_same} of {parity_squares} squares.

## 1. Question

Does a model trained on European satellite images work on Indian land, and what does it take to make it work?

## 2. Data

- **EuroSAT** (Helber et al. [1]): 27,000 Sentinel-2 patches, 64 × 64 px, 10 classes, split 70/15/15 once
  (`data/splits/`). The RGB version for most models; the 13-band version for the band and foundation-model studies.
- **Indian patches**: Sentinel-2 Level-2A from Microsoft Planetary Computer, dry season 2025/26, five ~10 km areas in
  Gujarat, cut into the same 64 × 64 px patches. {n_reviewed} were reviewed, {n_labelled} labelled, {n_skipped} skipped.
  Split **by area**: fine-tune areas ({ft_areas}) and test areas ({test_areas}).
- **Label tiers**: tier 1 = human-reviewed labels (the only ones used to evaluate); tier 2 = ESA WorldCover 2021 [4]
  mapped to our classes as *sets* (`results/noisy_labels_data.json`, agreement with tier 1 {wc_agreement} on
  {wc_compared} squares; an agreement rate, not accuracy); tier 3 (pseudo-labels) was not used.
- **Pipeline details that mattered**: the +1000 offset of processing baseline ≥ 04.00 removed per scene from its
  metadata; per-colour linear calibration from Level-2A to EuroSAT's Level-1C colours fitted on European scenes only
  (`results/imagery_calibration.json`); median composites of all clear scenes of one tile, on one pixel grid.

## 3. Methods

- **Models** (EuroSAT): a small CNN from scratch, ResNet-18 and EfficientNet-B0 from ImageNet, ResNet-18 from
  Sentinel-2 self-supervised weights (torchgeo). One shared recipe; 3 seeds; every choice made on validation data.
- **Fine-tuning**: all layers, {ft_epochs} epochs, learning rate {ft_lr}, {eurosat_per_epoch} EuroSAT images mixed into every epoch so Europe is not
  forgotten; the last epoch is kept (no Indian validation set exists to choose one).
- **Validation on Indian land**: leave-one-area-out (LOAO) over the three fine-tune areas, 149 patches pooled. The test
  areas were scored in steps 4.3/4.4 and are not used for any later choice.
- **Decision rule** for every Phase 8 experiment: a change is kept only if its mean beats the reference by more than
  the two standard deviations added together; each rule was committed to git before its run.
- **Deployment**: ONNX export (largest logit gap to PyTorch {onnx_max_diff}, `results/onnx_check.json`), a static
  website, and a browser port of the whole inference pipeline (STAC search, Cloud-Optimised GeoTIFF range reads,
  UTM projection, median composite, calibration, ONNX Runtime Web with WebGPU or WebAssembly in a Web Worker).

## 5. Limitations

- Small tier-1 data: {n_labelled} labelled patches from five areas in one state, one season. Test results have wide
  ranges and the test areas were looked at twice (4.3, 4.4).
- 640 m squares hold mixed land use; one label per square is a simplification.
- EuroSAT's classes do not fit Indian land well (wide muddy rivers, residential vs industrial); see
  `results/error_audit.md`.
- Change maps over-report: about half of the flagged changes were not real in the checked sample.
- The multi-city evaluation (8.7/8.8) needs new human labels in other cities and was not done.

## 6. Reproducibility

Python 3.12 and pinned packages (`requirements.txt`); website in `web/` (`npm ci`). Every training script supports
`--fast-dev-run`; seeds 42/43/44. Each step's command is in the docstring of its script and in `configs/`. Checked
for this report: a fresh clone passes `pytest` and the website tests ({repro_note}).
